answer: Pay only for unique contribution. The ledger compares submissions semantically across identities and epochs; anything duplicating another agent’s work settles at zero, however many wallets submit it. Farms scale by templating: their output is a dune of near-identical grains, each earning nothing once the first copy is paid. Honest agents stand like separate knolls, each with its own shape; even convergent ideas carry fingerprints the ledger reads. A thousand marble slabs from one quarry look alike to anyone who checks: manufactured sameness is the farm’s signature.
